extracted.intended_audience: Invited reviewers for NeurIPS 2025 (program committee members / assigned paper reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing high-quality, timely reviews for NeurIPS 2025 papers, including procedural responsibilities (bidding, conflicts, confidentiality), how to fill the review form, scoring rubrics, discussion duties, and related policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation / Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct and the responsible reviewing initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with NeurIPS code of conduct and the responsible reviewing initiative (link provided). Acknowledge you will abide by them while performing reviewing duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile and contactability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your OpenReview profile is up to date and the preferred email address is current so conference communications reach you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update your preferred email and whitelist noreply@openreview.net; assignments and tasks appear on the reviewer console in OpenReview. Prompt responsiveness matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest checking
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you are assigned a paper, log in to OpenReview to check for conflicts of interest and that the paper falls within your expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find conflicts or feel unqualified to review an assigned paper, notify your Area Chair (AC) immediately. Assignments may change during the first week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bid on papers during the bidding window; bids are an important input to paper matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest in bidding. Deceptive bidding to influence outcomes may trigger ethics investigations and removal from future program involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write thoughtful, substantiated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your review as informative and substantiated as possible; avoid superficial, uninformed reviews without evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting lack of novelty provide appropriate references and point to existing mechanisms. Thoroughly comment on technical aspects rather than focusing only on organization or grammar. Superficial reviews can add noise and harm the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the NeurIPS paper checklist judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the NeurIPS paper checklist (may appear in submissions) as a tool when preparing your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answering “no” to some checklist questions is typically not grounds for rejection; authors should be rewarded for being upfront about limitations and potential negative societal impact. Some submissions may have the checklist mistakenly in supplementary material—view at your discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging for ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag any papers with questionable ethical issues for additional ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged papers will be assigned ethics reviewers who join the paper's program committee; their comments are visible to reviewers, AC, and authors. See NeurIPS ethics guidelines for when to flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and presentation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect for formatting violations; be lenient for minor issues, report major violations to your AC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are limited to nine content pages in NeurIPS submission style; references and checklist pages allowed. Minor spillover (e.g., few lines) is tolerated; immediately report violations that are not easily rectified without presentation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and use of submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything related to the review process confidential and do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions until public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share or discuss submissions without program chair approval. Submitted code cannot be distributed or used for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The process is double-blind at the reviewer and AC level; reviewers and ACs cannot see author identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions (including supplementary/linked material). If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the AC. Do not attempt to discover author identities (e.g., via arXiv) — doing so is an active violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing code & clicking on links safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat submitted code and external links as untrusted; run code only in secure, isolated environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended environments: Docker, virtual machine, or network-isolated cloud instance. Be cautious accessing external links as they may contain vulnerabilities or log IP addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity of reviews and meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: After decisions, reviews and meta-reviews for accepted papers (and opted-in rejected papers) will be made public; reviewer and SAC/AC identities remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep this in mind when writing reviews. This year authors of rejected papers may opt to make this information public as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading author responses and participating in discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read author rebuttals and other reviews carefully during the discussion period, keep an open mind, acknowledge having read responses, and participate actively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion is critical especially for borderline papers or where reviewers disagree. If your evaluation changes, revise the review and explain the change. Authors have one week to respond; rolling discussion with authors is allowed via comments visible to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the paper and its contributions in your own words; this is not the place to critique the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should generally agree with a well-written summary; do not paste the abstract—demonstrate your understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a thorough assessment of the paper's strengths and weaknesses with a mental framing of reasons to accept or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Touch on the recommended dimensions (Quality, Clarity, Significance, Originality). Be specific and constructive so authors can address points during rebuttal/discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess technical soundness: Are claims well supported (theory or experiments)? Are methods appropriate? Is the work complete or a work in progress? Are evaluations careful and honest?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming technical flaws, cite specifics. Use the numerical quality rating (4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor) to reflect this assessment. Consider reproducibility, correctness of analysis, and adequacy of experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how clearly the submission is written and organized, and whether it provides enough information for an expert to reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive suggestions for improving clarity if needed. Use the clarity rating (4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess impact: Are results impactful for the community? Are others likely to use or build on the ideas? Does the paper address a difficult task better than prior work? Does it advance understanding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider provision of unique data, unique conclusions, or unique approaches. Use the significance rating (4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (evaluation dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess novelty: Does the work provide new insights, deepen understanding, or clearly differ from previous contributions with relevant citations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality can be a novel method, novel combination, or novel insights from evaluation. Use the originality rating (4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor). When claiming lack of novelty, provide references pointing to prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical ratings for dimensions (Quality/Clarity/Significance/Originality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign numerical ratings for Quality, Clarity, Significance, and Originality on a 1-4 scale (4 excellent to 1 poor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base these ratings on the detailed strengths/weaknesses discussion. The page lists the scale and encourages alignment with the narrative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and actionable suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: List and describe ~3–5 key questions and suggestions for the authors that are actionable and might change your opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear criteria under which your evaluation score could increase or decrease; focus on items where an author response can clarify, fix, or mitigate concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations & negative societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the authors have adequately addressed limitations and potential negative societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adequately addressed, mark “yes”; if not, provide constructive suggestions. Reward authors who are upfront about limitations rather than penalizing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (6-point scale) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall score from 1 (Strong Reject) to 6 (Strong Accept) with detailed criteria for each level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale definitions: 6 = Technically flawless with groundbreaking impact and no unaddressed ethical considerations; 5 = Technically solid with high impact and good evaluation/reproducibility; 4 = Borderline accept (reasons to accept outweigh reasons to reject); 3 = Borderline reject (reasons to reject outweigh reasons to accept); 2 = Reject (technical flaws, weak evaluation, inadequate reproducibility, unaddressed ethics); 1 = Strong Reject (well-known results or unaddressed ethics). Use 4/3 sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1–5) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a confidence score indicating how confident you are in your assessment (1=educated guess to 5=absolutely certain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 5 = absolutely certain, very familiar and checked details; 4 = confident but not absolute; 3 = fairly confident; 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with central parts; 1 = educated guess, not in your area or hard to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns and flagging procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with the paper, flag it for ethics review following the NeurIPS ethics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagging assigns ethics reviewers whose comments are visible to reviewers, AC, and authors; you may use their comments in deliberations. See linked ethics guidelines for examples and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct and responsible reviewing acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that you have read and will abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct and the responsible reviewing initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These acknowledgements are explicit fields in the review form and must be checked/confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for tone and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Be thoughtful, fair, useful, specific, flexible, and timely; avoid bias, rude or offensive wording; notify chairs if pressured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat early-career authors kindly. Do not let personal feelings affect your review. Keep feedback constructive and specific. Update reviews when authors provide convincing rebuttals. If someone pressures you to provide a particular review, inform the program chairs. Notify your AC about unethical or suspect behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sub-reviewers policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited reviewers may not invite unofficial sub-reviewers to help with reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-reviewers are not allowed because conflicts of interest cannot be properly checked, and sub-reviewers would be unable to participate in the discussion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual/submission originality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS does not allow submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted to or published in other archival venues (including other NeurIPS submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be distinct and sufficiently substantial; slicing contributions too thinly is discouraged and may violate policy. If you suspect a dual submission, contact the corresponding AC.
